First Team All-Big East (2012) }} '''Jae Crowder''' (born July 6, 1990 in [[Villa Rica, Georgia]]) is an [[United States|American]] [[college basketball]] player. Listed at 6'6" (1.98 m), the [[small forward|forward]] currently plays for the [[Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball|Marquette Golden Eagles]] in the [[Big East Conference]]. Prior to Marquette, Crowder played junior college basketball for [[Howard College|Howard County Junior College]]. Along with helping Howard win its first ever [[NJCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|national men's college basketball title]], Crowder was also selected as the 2009-10 NJCAA Player of the Year.{{cite web|title=Jae Crowder Profile|url=http://www.gomarquette.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/crowder_jae00.html|work=Marquette University Official Athletic Site|publisher=Marquette University|accessdate=7 March 2012}} Some [[Basketball statistics|basketball statisticians]] believe Crowder was statistically the best all-around player during the [[2010–11 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2010-2011 season]].{{cite news|last=Miller|first=Mike|title=Marquette may have the nation’s best all-around player|url=http://beyondthearc.nbcsports.com/2011/07/19/marquette-may-have-the-nations-best-all-around-player/|accessdate=7 March 2012|newspaper=NBC Sports|date=19 July 2011}} On January 1, 2011, Crowder recorded a career high 29 points and 8 rebounds in a game against the [[West Virginia Mountaineers men's basketball|West Virginia Mountaineers]].{{cite news|title=Crowder comes out of nowhere to lead Marquette|url=http://articles.chicagotribune.com/2011-01-06/sports/ct-spt-0107-marquette-jae-crowder-bas20110106_1_corey-crowder-golden-eagles-marquette-s-big-east|accessdate=7 March 2012|newspaper=Chicago Tribune|date=6 January 2011}} ==Honors== In March 2012, Crowder was named First Team All-Big East as a unanimous choice alongside teammate [[Darius Johnson-Odom]].{{cite news|title=Crowder, Johnson-Odom Named All-BIG EAST First Team|url=http://www.gomarquette.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/030412aaa.html|accessdate=7 March 2012|newspaper=GoMarquette.com|date=4 March 2012}} On March 6th, the conference announced that he had been awarded [[Big East Player of the Year]]. He is the first and only Marquette basketball player to have earned Player of the Year for the Big East Conference.{{cite web|title=Crowder named BIG EAST Player of the Year|url=http://www.gomarquette.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/030612aab.html|work=Marquette University Official Athletic Site|publisher=Marquette University|accessdate=7 March 2012}} Crowder also earned distinction as the [[NABC Player of the Year#State Farm Junior College Player of the Year|State Farm Junior College Player of the Year]] for the 2009-2010 season, prior to his transfer to Marquette.{{cite web|title=Player of the Year Awards|url=http://www.nabc.org/awards/poy|work=Awards - NABC|publisher=National Association of Basketball Coaches|accessdate=7 March 2012}} ==Personal life== Crowder graduated from Villa Rica High School in Villa Rica, GA, where he also played [[quarterback]] for the school's [[American football|football]] team. Crowder's father, [[Corey Crowder|Corey]], played in the NBA for the [[Utah Jazz]].{{cite web|title=Corey Crowder NBA & ABA Statistics|url=http://www.basketball-reference.com/players/c/crowdco01.html|publisher=Basketball-Reference.com|accessdate=7 March 2012}} He is currently majoring in [[Communication Studies]] at Marquette's [[Diederich College of Communication]]. ==See also== *[[NABC Player of the Year#State Farm Junior College Player of the Year|State Farm Junior College Player of the Year]] *[[Big East Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year]] ==Notes== {{reflist}} {{Big East Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year navbox}} {{Persondata | NAME = Crowder, Jae | ALTERNATIVE NAMES = | SHORT DESCRIPTION = American basketball player | DATE OF BIRTH = July 6, 1990 | PLACE OF BIRTH = Carrollton, Georgia | DATE OF DEATH = | PLACE OF DEATH = }} {{DEFAULTSORT:Crowder, Jae}} [[Category:1990 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:Basketball players from Georgia (U.S. state)]] [[Category:Junior college men's basketball players in the United States]] [[Category:Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball players]] [[Category:People from Villa Rica, Georgia]] [[Category:Small forwards]]
